title: Japan Auction Price vs FOB vs CIF: What Overseas Vehicle Buyers Are Actually Comparing
description: Understand the difference between Japan auction price, vehicle price, FOB and CIF so overseas vehicle buyers can compare offers on the same basis.
content:
Many overseas buyers think two Japanese vehicle quotes are directly comparable when they are actually using different price bases. A low auction or vehicle price can become expensive once compulsory Japan-side and shipping costs are added.
Auction or hammer priceThis is the winning auction bid. It normally does not represent the buyer's complete payable amount because auction house fees, agent costs, inland transport and document costs may still apply.
Japan vehicle priceA dealer or exporter may quote the vehicle price including some charges but excluding others. Always ask exactly what is inside the number rather than assuming it is equivalent to an auction invoice.
FOBFOB generally moves the comparison closer to an export-ready Japan-side basis, but sellers can still package different services into their calculations. Confirm the named port and included cost lines.
CIFCIF commonly includes freight and insurance to an agreed destination, but destination taxes, clearance, registration and local costs may remain outside the quote. The buyer should compare the same incoterm and same destination.
The practical ruleBefore choosing the lowest number, put every offer into one table with vehicle, Japan fees, inland transport, documents, freight, insurance, destination costs and dealer margin. The cheapest headline price is not always the best buy.

title: How to Read a Japanese Auction Sheet: Grade 4.5, Interior A and Repair Marks
description: A practical explanation of Japanese auction grades, interior grades and why buyers should read the full auction sheet instead of relying on one grade number.
content:
A Japanese auction grade is useful, but it is not a complete condition report. Buyers should treat the grade as a starting point and then read the inspector comments, body map and interior evaluation before making a commercial decision.
What a grade such as 4.5 meansA higher grade generally indicates a better overall condition level, but standards and interpretation can vary between auction groups and individual vehicles. A 4.5 does not automatically mean perfect bodywork or zero repairs.
Why the interior grade mattersInterior grades help buyers distinguish vehicles that may look similar externally but have very different cabin wear. For premium vehicles, smoke odor, stains, seat wear or trim damage can significantly affect resale quality.
Read the body mapScratch, dent, paint, replacement and repair notations can reveal where future reconditioning cost may appear. Buyers should not approve an auction vehicle from the headline grade alone.
Inspector comments are commercially importantComments can mention warning lights, corrosion, noise, odors, repairs, missing equipment or other issues that do not fit neatly into the overall grade. A translated or clearly explained sheet is therefore part of good buyer-side verification.
Use the auction sheet together with market economicsCondition only matters in context. A cheaper vehicle with expensive reconditioning can be worse for the buyer than a higher-priced unit with stronger evidence and cleaner condition.

Check condition evidenceFor auction vehicles, review the auction sheet and grade, but also look at the underlying notes and damage markings. For dealer stock, ask what inspection evidence is available and whether repairs or replacement panels are disclosed.
Verify the commercial stackA useful quote should distinguish the vehicle price from Japan-side fees, inland logistics, documentation and any shipping service. This makes supplier comparison far more reliable than comparing a single headline number.
Confirm seller identity and payment beneficiaryBefore sending funds, verify the company identity, invoice issuer and bank beneficiary. The payment details should match the verified commercial counterparty or be clearly explained in writing.
Check destination requirements separatelyImport eligibility, inspection, tax and registration requirements can change by destination and by vehicle age or specification. Treat those as a separate verification gate rather than assuming every Japan-market Prado qualifies automatically.

title: Japan Vehicle Price vs. Real Japan-Side Cost: What Overseas Buyers Should Compare
description: Why two Japanese vehicle offers with the same headline price may have very different real costs, and what buyers should ask before comparing quotes.
content:
A vehicle advertised at JPY 4,000,000 is not automatically a JPY 4,000,000 procurement. Buyers comparing Japan offers should compare the same price basis and the same included scope.
Headline vehicle priceThis is the starting point only. Confirm whether it is tax-inclusive or tax-exclusive, whether it is retail or dealer pricing, and whether mandatory local charges are already included.
Dealer, auction or sourcing feesDifferent routes have different compulsory costs. Auction fees, agent fees or dealer handling charges should be separated from the vehicle price instead of hidden in an unclear total.
Domestic transportA vehicle far from the export point may require significant Japan-side transport. If the buyer chooses the port based on vehicle location, that can change the commercial structure.
Inspection and evidenceWhen independent checking, photographs, video or document verification are requested, these services have a real cost. Buyers should know whether they are included or optional.
Export documentation and port scopeWho handles deregistration, export certificate preparation, customs filing, port delivery and shipping must be explicit. 'Buyer arranges shipping' does not automatically answer who prepares every Japan-side document.
Payment, currency and contingencyBank charges, payment processing, FX exposure and changes between quote and purchase can affect the final amount. A quote should state its currency and validity period.
Compare like with likeWhen JPNentry quotes, the goal is to define the basis, inclusions, exclusions and responsibilities so the buyer can compare the offer properly. A lower headline price is not better if essential Japan-side costs appear later.
Send one requirementIf you have a live vehicle or parts requirement, send the exact specification, quantity, target price and currency, destination and timing. We will verify the route before presenting it as a commercial option.
